question: A per-OP error budget. The engine(F32) vs llama.cpp(F32) residual on qwen2.5-3b is 4.07e-6 after every REDUCTION was matched exactly (the 18-site sweep). Nothing said whether that 4.07e-6 is the composed consequence of ops already measured, or an op nobody has looked at. A per-model number cannot tell those apart: a fully-explained floor and a missing op both print one number.
method: engine/src/opdump.rs captures the vectors the engine's OWN forward pass produced (silu gate pre-activations, attention scores, rope inputs/outputs) -- not synthesised. 21168 vectors, 26.5 MB, 36 layers x 12 positions.
engine/tools/probe_op_budget.c measures each op's relative L2 AND bit agreement between the reference kernel and the engine's formulation, on those vectors.

the tool's transcriptions of ggml_v_expf / ggml_v_silu / ggml_vec_soft_max_f32 are verified BIT-IDENTICAL against the real exported ggml_vec_silu_f32 and ggml_vec_soft_max_f32 in libggml-cpu.so (--verify), with a control proving the check discriminates.
composition: random walk over independent roundings. An ASSUMPTION, and it is tested below by porting the largest per-op error and re-measuring end to end.
reference: cached at /tmp/opencode/t31/work/llama-{capital,moon}.ref -- NOT re-run, so every column shares one oracle

per_op.note: relative L2 of the engine's formulation vs the reference kernel, on 21168 real activation vectors

silu.reference: ggml_vec_silu_f32 -> ggml_v_silu -> ggml_v_expf (the ARM polynomial, ~1.95 ulp)
silu.why_small: the polynomial is within ~2 ulp of libm, so a 37% bit disagreement is a ~4e-8 effect

softmax.reference: ggml_vec_soft_max_f32: expf is the POLYNOMIAL, the sum is 8 f32 lanes reduced as a tree into a DOUBLE, and ops.cpp:5549 does 1.0/sum in double then scales
softmax.engine: libm expf, sum in SEQUENTIAL f32, then each element divided by the f32 sum
softmax.why_small: three wrong things that all cancel to ~1e-7 at these sequence lengths (max 12)

rope.reference: ggml_compute_forward_rope_flt (ops.cpp:5953) + ggml_rope_cache_init (ops.cpp:5846): f32 powf, f32 ladder, sinf/cosf of an f32
rope.engine: f64 pow, f64 ladder, f64 sin/cos narrowed at the end
rope.verdict: THE ONE REAL FINDING -- 5600x the size of the other two, and the only op here that is wrong by more than round-off

composition_and_why_it_is_wrong.verdict: OVERSHOOTS by 3 orders of magnitude, so the random-walk composition is WRONG, not the ops. An op whose error is a coherent ROTATION (rope) does not accumulate like independent roundings: every head and every layer gets the SAME angle error, so it cancels instead of adding.
composition_and_why_it_is_wrong.this_was_not_left_as_an_assumption: it was tested by porting rope and re-measuring end to end

rope_port.what_changed: theta_scale and the frequency ladder in f32, carrying theta as the reference does rather than recomputing pos*cur, and BOTH products contracted into an fma (rotate_pairs is compiled into an -O3 libggml-cpu.so, which contracts; nothing in the source says so)
rope_port.bit_identical_to: ggml on 15936/15936 golden values across n_dims {8,32,64,80,96,128,256}, pos {0,1,7,137}, 3 freq_bases, both NORMAL and NEOX
rope_port.before: f64 ladder, no fma: 5267/15936 bits differ
rope_port.after_f32_but_no_fma: 1822/15936 bits differ -- i.e. 93.75% bit-identical passes a 1e-6 tolerance test, which is why the original test was a tolerance and looked justified
rope_port.END_TO_END_EFFECT: NONE. 4.0668e-06 -> 4.5492e-06 -> 4.0668e-06 on the worst position: the f32 port is strictly more correct and moved the logits by nothing. argmax 17/17 throughout.

the_finding: A 2.1e-4 per-op error that is bit-exactly fixed does not move the end-to-end residual. That is the answer to the question the budget was built to answer, and it is the opposite of what the budget predicted: the 4.07e-6 is NOT the sum of the per-op errors, because the dominant per-op error is a coherent rotation that cancels. So the per-op budget, as a composition device, does not work -- and the next question is not 'which op is left' but 'what is the 4.07e-6 made of, given that the ops are now all at round-off'.
rope_golden_toy_width: engine/tests/data/rope_golden.bin was entirely n_dims=8 -- FOUR ladder rungs. The f64/f32 question was worth 1 bit in 144 there, so a 2.1e-4 per-op error sat behind a golden that printed OK. tools/dump_rope.c now sweeps 7 widths including real head dims; the revert is caught 5267/15936 instead of 1/144. Same failure shape as the ggml_vec_dot_f32 tail (tick 32): a toy width is the only thing that cannot see the bug.

artifacts.tool: engine/tools/probe_op_budget.c (--verify links libggml-cpu.so; --control runs with no model)
artifacts.capture: engine/src/opdump.rs, inert unless SLOW_OP_DUMP names a file
artifacts.test: engine/tests/rope_parity.rs, now 2 tests: the original 1e-6 gate kept, plus bit equality

bugs_of_my_own: the activation writer wrote `n.to_le_bytes()` on a u64 -- EIGHT bytes where the reader expected four, so every record after the first was skewed and the reader reported 'slot 1052389815 >= 4'. Silent and total.
the slot-3 branch passed the same buffer as src and dst to eng_rope, which writes dst[i] before reading src[i+half]; it reported rel L2 9.46e-01 that meant nothing.

the verdict thresholds were INVERTED: measured/predicted = 0.0016 was being printed as 'consistent: budget explains it', when a ratio that far below 1 means the budget OVERSHOOTS. The tool agreed with whatever it was told.

my first silu transcription used the vector polynomial in the scalar tail; upstream's tail is ggml_silu_f32, which is libm expf. Caught by --verify against the real exported kernel, which is the only reason that check was worth writing.
NaN payloads counted as bit differences, which is not a kernel difference.
